summary: The 15 tier C island realms of the Islands of the South: the sea's living, the guest-right, old tales, priests at the quays, the island's rule, two shores, navigators, life under a protector and the storm years. Modules I1 to I9.

island_markets_spirit.name: Island Markets
island_markets_spirit.desc: Boats from three isles meet in the lee of a reef each full moon, and the haggling goes on until the tide turns.

fishing_fleets.name: The Fishing Fleets
fishing_fleets.desc: A hundred sails leave the beaches at dawn and spread across the water like gulls.

guest_right.name: The Guest-Right
guest_right.desc: No guest is turned from a door. He is fed, warmed and housed for three days before anyone asks his name.

reef_lamps.name: Lamps on the Reefs
reef_lamps.desc: Tallow lamps on poles mark the dangerous reefs, and ships that once smashed on the rocks now pass them in the dark.

old_tales.name: Old Tales of the Isles
old_tales.desc: A choir sings the island's oldest songs to every ship, and sailors carry them away to ports the islanders will never see.

healers_at_the_quays.name: Healers at the Quays
healers_at_the_quays.desc: Healers in grey robes tend the sick on the quay and feed the hungry.

speakers_council.name: Council of the Isle
speakers_council.desc: The speakers settle quarrels in public, and their rulings are carved on the council stones.

chiefs_moot.name: The Chiefs' Moot
chiefs_moot.desc: Every chief speaks in turn beneath the great tree, and the strongest voice sets the course.

sea_kings_law.name: The Sea-King's Law
sea_kings_law.desc: Keep the peace on shore, share the catch and follow the king's boat.

island_navigators_spirit.name: Island Navigators
island_navigators_spirit.desc: The navigators read the sea by the swell, the stars and the flight of birds.

southern_seas.name: Masters of the Southern Seas
southern_seas.desc: The best navigators in the south, and no one argues.

protectors_favour.name: The Protector's Favour
protectors_favour.desc: The protector has noticed that the island is useful, and is pleased.

far_from_the_war.name: Far From the Kings' Wars
far_from_the_war.desc: The harbour is closed to warships and the boats stay in their sheds. The island wants only to be left alone.

island_feast.title: An Island Feast
island_feast.desc: Boats from three islands have drawn up on the beach, and the visitors are hungry. The elders of [ROOT.GetName] look at their stores, look at each other and decide how much of the island's wealth should go into a pot.

the_reef_singers.title: The Reef Singers
the_reef_singers.desc: Old fishers sing of a reef where drowned voices call ships onto the rocks. The song is known on every island of the south, and the islanders of [ROOT.GetName] argue over whether the custom it teaches should be kept.

options.name: Honour the old custom: no boat at night

focuses.name: [ROOT.GetName] Keeps Its Shores
focuses.desc: The islanders of [ROOT.GetName] have always lived by the shore: fishing it, salting it, mending its boats and watching its weather. Today the elders gather on the beach, count the nets and decide what the island will do with another year.

focuses.name: Nets and Boats
focuses.desc: New nets are knotted in the long evenings, and the boat-sheds ring with the sound of adzes. The fishers of [ROOT.GetName] ask for a proper slip and a shipwright who has seen more than one kind of hull.

focuses.name: The Salt Pans
focuses.desc: Shallow pans are scraped out behind the dunes, and the sun does the rest. Salt is the island's oldest wealth, and every trader who has ever called at [ROOT.GetName] has bought some.

focuses.name: The Pearl Divers
focuses.desc: Divers go down on a single breath with a stone in their hands and come up with their pockets full of grey and silver. A good pearl is worth more than a boat, and the divers know it.

focuses.name: Boatwrights of the Isles
focuses.desc: The boatwrights of [ROOT.GetName] build low, broad hulls with outriggers that no storm has ever turned over. Visitors from richer lands copy them and call them their own.

focuses.name: Island Markets
focuses.desc: Each full moon, boats from three isles meet in the lee of a reef and trade. Salt, pearls, dried fish and woven mats change hands, and the haggling goes on until the tide turns.

focuses.name: The Fishing Fleets
focuses.desc: Every dawn, a hundred sails leave the beaches of [ROOT.GetName] and spread across the water like gulls. They return at dusk with enough for the whole island and enough over to sell.

focuses.name: The Guest-Right
focuses.desc: No wrecked sailor, no stray fisherman and no weary traveller has ever been turned from a door in [ROOT.GetName]. A guest is fed, warmed and housed for three days before anyone asks his name.

focuses.name: Island Feasts
focuses.desc: Visitors arrive in ones and twos, then in boatloads. The islanders of [ROOT.GetName] roast what they have, pour what they have and sing until the moon has set.

focuses.name: Shelter for the Wrecked
focuses.desc: A reef-wardens' hut is raised on every headland, stocked with dry blankets, salt fish and a signal horn. When a ship goes down, the islanders pull the survivors ashore before the tide has turned.

focuses.name: Lamps on the Reefs
focuses.desc: Tallow lamps are hung on poles above the dangerous reefs, lit at dusk by children who are paid in sweet cakes. Ships that once smashed on the rocks now pass them in the dark.

focuses.name: Carry It to Gala
focuses.desc: The islanders have a saying: when the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, carry them to Gala. A boat is fitted out with a scribe, a drum and a bundle of the island's oldest songs.

effects.tooltip: When the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, carry them to Gala.

focuses.name: A Welcome on Every Shore
focuses.desc: From the largest island to the smallest skerry, every beach in [ROOT.GetName] has a fire, a boat-shed and someone to keep the door open. Sailors say they would rather be wrecked here than anywhere else.

focuses.name: Old Tales of the Isles
focuses.desc: The old women of [ROOT.GetName] sit in the lee of the boat-sheds and tell the tales their grandmothers told them. Nobody has ever written them down, and nobody who has heard them forgets them.

focuses.name: The Reef Singers
focuses.desc: Old fishers sing a song about a reef where drowned voices call ships onto the rocks. Everyone knows the tune, and no one will say on which reef it began.

focuses.name: Keepers of Old Names
focuses.desc: The names of stars, currents, winds and reefs are taught to the children as soon as they can speak. Learned visitors take notes and are astonished at how much has been remembered.

focuses.name: Songs for Visitors
focuses.desc: A choir is formed to sing the island's songs to every ship that calls. The tunes are simple, the words are old, and sailors carry them away to ports the islanders will never see.

focuses.name: Priests at the Quays
focuses.desc: Grey-robed priests from the north have begun to meet the ships, offering blessings, bread and news. The islanders of [ROOT.GetName] are polite to them, and a little curious.

focuses.name: Welcome the Healers
focuses.desc: The healers of the Deliverer ask for a house on the quay, where the sick can be tended and the hungry fed. [ROOT.GetName] gives them a building, a well and a cautious welcome.

focuses.name: Send Them on Their Way
focuses.desc: The elders of [ROOT.GetName] thank the priests for their kindness, give them a good meal and put them on the next boat out. There is no insult in it, only the island's way of keeping what is its own.

focuses.name: Close the Houses of the Isle
focuses.desc: The house on the quay is shuttered, the well sealed and the healers' ledgers surrendered to the elders. The island's kindness has limits, and the elders have chosen where they lie.

focuses.name: The Rule of [ROOT.GetName]
focuses.desc: Who rules an island? The people of [ROOT.GetName] have answered that question in different ways at different times, and each answer has its supporters. The elders call a gathering on the beach to settle it once more.

focuses.name: The Speakers' Council
focuses.desc: A circle of speakers is chosen from the island's villages, one for every ten hearths. They sit on a ring of flat stones, and whoever holds the talking-shell speaks.

focuses.name: The Chief's Hall
focuses.desc: A great thatched hall rises above the beach, with carved posts and a hearth that has not gone out in living memory. The chief of [ROOT.GetName] sits at its head and hears every dispute.

focuses.name: A Sea-King
focuses.desc: One captain has led the island's boats to victory so often that the folk have begun to call him king. He wears a crown of shells and a cloak of dyed bark, and nobody laughs.

focuses.name: Council of the Isle
focuses.desc: The speakers settle the island's quarrels in public, and their rulings are carved on the council stones. No one remembers a ruling that was not obeyed.

focuses.name: The Chiefs' Moot
focuses.desc: Every chief of every village sits in a ring beneath the great tree and speaks his mind in turn. When they have all spoken, the strongest voice sets the course, and the rest fall in.

focuses.name: The Sea-King's Law
focuses.desc: The sea-king's law is short: keep the peace on shore, share the catch and follow the king's boat. It is enforced by his captains, and most of the time they do not need to raise their voices.

focuses.name: Two Shores
focuses.desc: The bigger islands have a far shore as well as a near one, and a heart of hills between them. [ROOT.GetName] sends surveyors inland with rope and stakes, and learns how much of its own land it has never seen.

focuses.name: Roads Across the Isle
focuses.desc: A track of packed coral and sand is laid across the island, from the near shore to the far. Porters, mules and carts can now cross in a day what once took three.

focuses.name: The Inland Fields
focuses.desc: Terraced fields climb the interior slopes, watered by channels cut from the highland streams. Taro, yams and breadfruit fill the stores, and for the first time the island feeds itself from the middle.

focuses.name: One Isle, One Law
focuses.desc: Shore and hill, fisher and farmer, come under one law at last. The elders of [ROOT.GetName] declare the island one realm, and the people feast for three days to celebrate.

focuses.name: Island Navigators
focuses.desc: The navigators of [ROOT.GetName] read the sea by the swell, the stars and the flight of birds. They cross open water without chart or compass, and they have never been known to miss a landfall.

focuses.name: Charts of the Southern Seas
focuses.desc: Charts woven from palm-ribs and shells record the currents, reefs and island-chains of the southern seas. A navigator can read the whole weave at a glance.

focuses.name: Galleys of the Isles
focuses.desc: Long galleys with a hundred paddles and a high stern take shape in the boat-sheds of [ROOT.GetName]. They are built for speed, for the open sea and for crews that sing while they row.

focuses.name: Hulls for Hire
focuses.desc: The kings of the West are looking for hulls to cross the sea, and the boatwrights of [ROOT.GetName] have a dozen to hire. Western agents arrive with silver and leave with promises.

focuses.name: Navigators for Gala
focuses.desc: Gala sends word that it needs navigators who know the southern seas, and the best of [ROOT.GetName] sign on. They sail with a king's blessing and come home with strange stories.

focuses.name: Masters of the Southern Seas
focuses.desc: The navigators of [ROOT.GetName] are called the best in the south, and no one argues. Their boats have been to every shore and their charts hang in every harbour-house.

focuses.name: The Oath to the Protector
focuses.desc: The elders of [ROOT.GetName] sail to the protector's court, bearing shells, salt and a bundle of tally-sticks. They swear to keep the protector's peace, and are given a cloak of feathers in return.

focuses.name: A Loyal Isle
focuses.desc: The island makes itself useful to its protector: its boats carry the protector's goods, its fishers feed the protector's ports and its elders give the protector good counsel. The protector notices.

focuses.name: Our Own Shores
focuses.desc: Every beach of [ROOT.GetName] has belonged to the island since before the protector was born. The elders remind him of it, politely, in their best feathers.

focuses.name: The Storm Years
focuses.desc: Word arrives by every boat that the kings of the north and west are at war. The islanders of [ROOT.GetName] look out across the empty sea, count their stores and decide to keep the war on the far side of the horizon.

focuses.name: Far From the Kings' Wars
focuses.desc: The island declares that the wars of the great are not its wars. The harbour is closed to warships, the boats stay in their sheds, and the elders send word to every side that [ROOT.GetName] wants only to be left alone.

focuses.name: The Isles Stand Together
focuses.desc: Boats go out to every neighbouring island carrying a knotted cord, the island way of saying that peace is promised. [ROOT.GetName] and its neighbours agree to keep the peace between them for as long as the war lasts.

focuses.name: Ships for the Gathering Host
focuses.desc: When a host gathers against the dead, the isles can send it boats and men.

focuses.name: Watch the Southern Waves
focuses.desc: Whatever else the war brings, it may bring ships. Lookouts take their places on the headlands of [ROOT.GetName], and the boats are kept ready on their rollers.
